title: Machine-learning-guided search discovers and synthesizes the rare-earth-free magnet Fe₃CoB₂
summary: A feedback workflow combining machine learning, an adaptive genetic algorithm, first-principles calculations, and experiments identified and synthesized Fe₃CoB₂, a rare-earth-free magnetic compound. Magnetic measurements reported saturation polarization Js=1.39 T and anisotropy K1=1.2 MJ/m³, properties the authors describe as suitable for rare-earth-free permanent-magnet applications. This is a discovery and synthesis of a material compound; commercial performance or device readiness was not demonstrated.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided adaptive feedback with an adaptive genetic algorithm and first-principles calculations
organization: Ames Laboratory; Iowa State University; University of Nebraska–Lincoln; University of Texas at Austin; University of Tokyo; Yantai University; Zhejiang Agriculture and Forestry University

evidence.tested: A feedback workflow combining machine learning, an adaptive genetic algorithm, first-principles calculations, and experiments identified and synthesized Fe₃CoB₂, a rare-earth-free magnetic compound.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports an experimentally synthesized compound and magnetic measurements, but suitability is for potential rare-earth-free permanent-magnet applications; no commercial device demonstration is reported. The workflow combines ML with adaptive genetic search, DFT and human synthesis/measurement.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning screened and informed the material search, while adaptive genetic structure search and first-principles calculations guided candidates; researchers synthesized the selected compound and measured its magnetic properties. The discovery is attributed to the integrated workflow, not the ML model alone.
